_why: Role track for QUALITY INSPECTION / QC, authored under docs/profiling/role-pack-authoring-guide.md as Batch 2 part two's second pack. fam_other_craft stays the generic ISCO-minor-754 interview and is NOT touched; this pack belongs to fam_quality_inspection, which binds the NCO metal-inspection occupations directly (job_domain specificity 50 beats minor 30) -- 7543.2001 'Quality Inspector-forged, casted or machined components' and 7311.0500 'Viewer, Workshop / Examiner, Metal Working' -- so a machine-shop inspector gets inspection depth and every cloth examiner, footwear checker, electronics tester and rubber-line QC in the unit keeps the generic pack.
_scope: DIMENSIONAL AND VISUAL INSPECTION OF MACHINED, CAST, FORGED AND PRESSED METAL PARTS -- CMM, profile projector, height gauge and hand instruments, on the incoming, patrol, final and layout stages, with the PPAP / control plan / SPC / 8D paperwork the job is. The level ladder (Inspector / QC Engineer) is asked as inspection_level so the sheet can say which rung the worker stands on. Textile, footwear and wood grading, electronics functional testing and rubber/plastics line QC (7543.3001-3005, worksheet R4-b) are NOT bound here. The measuring instruments are asked on the SHARED measuring_tools key, and they are deliberately NOT detection terms on the descriptor: every machining trade owns a vernier, so only the words that belong to inspection alone -- CMM, profile projector, PPAP, SPC, control plan -- corroborate this role.
_depth: THE TIER GATE IS inspection_experience, asked FIRST, and it is QUALITY_INSPECTOR.tenureQuestionKey. It cannot be experience_years from qp_universal: phase order runs occupation_specific BEFORE universal_tail, so the universal answer does not exist yet when these items are selected -- gating on it is permanently false. Its options carry value_number ONLY. pack-registry.service.ts resolves valueText ?? valueNumber, so a value_text beside the number would turn every gte gate below into a string comparison that is false forever.
_budget: MAX_ENGINE_ASKS is 48 and qp_universal@4 spends at most 18. Tier 0 is 7 items, tier 1 (inspection_experience >= 2) adds 3, tier 2 (>= 5) adds 3 -- a senior walks 13, two fewer than the welder's 15. The three fresher items are gated inspection_experience <= 0, so a senior never sees them and a fresher, who fails both gte gates by construction, tops out at 7 + 3 = 10.
_sheet: SECTION B IS READ OFF THE RATIFIED QUALITY INSPECTOR REFERENCE RESUME (Anjali Verma, page 13), not invented. Its eight rows are Instruments, Standards, Materials inspected, Inspection stage, Documentation, Drawings, Least count worked to and Sector worked, and every one has a question here that fills it. Documentation carries SIX options because the page prints six (PPAP documents, Control plan, Inspection report, 8D / CAPA, SPC charts, Calibration register); trimming to the chip guideline's six-with-escape would have dropped a row value the page shows. Instruments offers the page's four (CMM, Profile projector, Height gauge, Surface roughness tester) plus 'Vernier aur micrometer', because a one-year patrol inspector holds those two and nothing else -- without the chip his instrument row would be empty; plug and ring gauges are left out to stay inside the chip count. Least count is a BANDED single_select (0.02 / 0.01 / 0.001 mm), the welder's plate ruling: the page prints one figure, 'Works to 0.001 mm least count', and a band renders as the page renders it. The three tier-2 items (inspection_cmm_work, inspection_rejection_work, inspection_audit_work) have NO sheet row -- the page has none and this pack does not invent one; they are matching data in worker_attributes. This pack has no case in role-sheet-parity.render.test.ts yet.
_keys: NO DIGITS IN ANY question_key OR option_key. Both regexes are ^[a-z_]+$, and slugKey REFUSES a key with a digit at runtime even where the corpus validator historically let it through -- one such key makes the whole pack unparseable. So ISO 9001 is iso_nine_thousand_one, 8D is eight_d_capa and 0.001 mm is point_zero_zero_one; THE LABEL KEEPS THE REAL TEXT, because the label is the worker's answer of record. material_worked, measuring_tools, drawing_reading and sector_worked are the SHARED keys other packs already use, deliberately: resume-degradation.ts sheds rows BY KEY (sector_worked first, material_worked trimmed) to keep a sheet on one page, and a private key would opt this trade out of that. Every other key carries the inspection_ prefix.
review_note: Drafted for owner review. Shop-floor vocabulary NOT yet corrected by a practising quality inspector -- see docs/registers/trade-content-ratification.md.
_fresher: Guideline section 11 #1: a fresher's Zone 4 is training, trade test, machines used in the ITI workshop and project work, and the History heading never renders empty. These three items are the ask half; resume-fresher-rows.ts, fed by this role's descriptor, is the render half. The KEYS are read literally by that file and must not be renamed; only the workshop VOCABULARY is trade-specific. The three prompts are the welder's verbatim, so they reuse its served text and its voice clips. A QC fresher comes out of an ITI machinist, turner or fitter workshop, so the machines are those -- plus the surface plate, the one workshop station that is inspection work.
